method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs
why_not_one_block_off: The chosen line is the centre of the corridor that is lettered in its own roadway on BOTH sheets. Sheet 50: 'AVE. J OR BROADWAY' is printed vertically inside the corridor whose block faces I read off the green ruler at native 1002.0 (east face of the block to the west) and 1305.0 (west face of the block to the east); centre 1153.5. Sheet 56: the same corridor is lettered 'AVE. J. OR BROADWAY' with '150 ft. wide' printed beside it; faces at native 1002.6 and 1306.3; centre 1154.5. Face-to-face width is 303.0 px on sheet 50 and 303.7 px on sheet 56 - the same corridor measured the same way, and the widest corridor on either sheet (the lettered 70' avenues on these sheets measure 211-213 px and the mid-block alley 62 px). ADDRESS RUNS. Sheet 50, the 26TH ST and 27TH ST runs: west of the line '...918 920 922 924' and '917 919 921 923' (900 block); east of it '1002 1004 1006 1008 1010 1012' and '1001 1003 1005 1007 1009 1011', continuing past the 20 ft alley as '1014 1016 1018 1020 1022 1024' (1000 block). Broadway's own frontage numbers on sheet 50 are 2510 2512 2514 2516 2518 2520 2522 2524 2526 2528 on its west face and 2509 2511 2513 2515 2517 2519 2521 2523 2525 2527 on its east face - the 2500 block, i.e. between 25TH and 26TH ST, which is inside sheet 50's street range (24-27). Sheet 56, the 27TH ST and 28TH ST runs: west of the line '901 903 905 907 909 911' and '913 915 917 919 921 923' (900 block); east of it '1001 1003 1006 1007 1009' (1000 block). Broadway's frontage numbers on sheet 56 are 2701 2703 ... 2727 and 2702 2704 ... 2728 - the 2700 block, between 27TH and 28TH ST, inside sheet 56's street range (27-30). So on both sheets this one corridor carries the 900-to-1000 block change, and the two sheets simply show different hundred-blocks OF Broadway itself (2500 vs 2700), which is exactly what two sheets stacked in the street direction must show. ONE BLOCK WEST is excluded: that is Ave I (Sealy) - lettered 'AVE. I OR SEALY' at the west edge of sheet 56 - and it carries the 800-to-900 change, not 900-to-1000. ONE BLOCK EAST is excluded: that is Avenue K, lettered 'AVENUE K' on both sheets (measured faces 2095.5/2308.8 on sheet 50, 2092.7/2305.4 on sheet 56), and it carries the 1000-to-1100 change - sheet 50 cand#3 shows '1102 1104 1106 1108 1110 1112' immediately east of it. Broadway is in any case unique on the island, so there is no lettered twin one block away. CANDIDATES REJECTED. None of the proposed candidates is a corridor at all. Sheet 50 cand#1 (native 1516) and cand#3 (native 2528) both cut through the interiors of blocks (cand#1 crosses the buildings at 1006-1008, cand#3 the block 2501-2527 / 1102-1112); sheet 56 cand#1 (native 846) likewise runs inside the 913-923 block. Every candidate sits about 360 px east of a real avenue, i.e. detection locked onto a repeated lot line. The values reported here are ruler-read avenue centres and are NOT among the candidates. CROSS-CHECK: Broadway gives a sheet50->sheet56 offset of +1.0 px; Avenue K measured independently gives -3.1 px and the 20 ft alley between them (centres 1699.9 and 1700.4) +0.5 px. The three agree to about 4 px, where a one-block error would be ~1010 px.
